name: Matbench v0.1 mp_is_metal
description: Predict whether a crystal is a metal (1) or not (0) according to its band gap calculated by density functional theory from its crystal structure (Matbench v0.1 task mp_is_metal, 106113 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 600 seconds.

sources.locator: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties

Dunn et al. (2020), Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm (npj Comput Mater): benchmark paper defining the tasks, the nested cross-validation and the metrics; Crossref title verified.
Task table of matbench_v0.1: matbench_mp_is_metal: classification/structure, is_metal, 106,113 samples..

requirements.datasets: matbench_mp_is_metal.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers, each exactly 0 or 1 (class labels; any other value is invalid). Every input is a dict with the keys lattice (the three lattice vectors in angstrom, a 3 x 3 list), species (the element symbol of every site) and frac_coords (the fractional coordinates of every site). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels (which equals the balanced accuracy), maximized.
notes: matbench_mp_is_metal.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

limitations: Leaders are graph neural networks and tuned ensembles; the leaderboard snapshot has no date.

The classification score is the ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels, which equals the balanced accuracy: the record is the leaderboard's best balanced accuracy (the page has a second column, probability ROC AUC, that this task does not use).
This task has 106k-133k structures: featurising them is slow, so a candidate must be efficient; the seed uses a cheap feature set.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

science_relevance.reason: Each cited paper has the prediction of the task's materials property from composition or structure as its main objective; the Matbench paper is a benchmark paper and is listed under extra_sources only.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify an inorganic crystal as a metal or a non-metal (DFT) from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Whether a material conducts is the first screen for electronic, photovoltaic and thermoelectric uses, and structure-based classifiers screen computed candidates cheaply.

papers.title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
papers.task_relation: The paper includes a metal-versus-semiconductor classification of Materials Project crystals; the task is the same classification on the Matbench subset with free choice of model.
papers.primary_goal: Learn crystal properties directly from the atomic connections of a structure, with a graph neural network trained on Materials Project DFT data (eight properties).
